question: Long-term daily use of stimulant laxatives such as senna is recommended as first-line maintenance therapy for chronic idiopathic constipation because they are the most effective class for sustained bowel regularity.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Although stimulant laxatives (senna, bisacodyl) are effective for occasional use, chronic daily use can impair enteric neuromuscular function (cathartic colon), induce melanosis coli, and create laxative dependence. Osmotic agents are safer for long-term maintenance.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Stimulant laxatives are not first-line for long-term constipation management. Chronic use risks cathartic colon (structural myenteric damage), melanosis coli, and physiological dependence. Dietary fibre, hydration, and osmotic laxatives (e.g., polyethylene glycol, lactulose) are the preferred agents for long-term maintenance.
